_readme: Claims ledger for the on-page legend. Every on-page claim has exactly one tag. Tags: shipped | specified | assumption | limit | human_gate. evidence_level: public (a public URL a visitor can open) | self_reported.

tags.shipped: Built and demonstrably in use or published. Needs a public link, or is marked self_reported.
tags.specified: Designed and written down, not (yet) implemented. The CV itself makes this distinction.
tags.assumption: Something the design relies on that has not been verified. Concepts that illustrate an idea sit here.
tags.limit: An evidence limitation: what cannot be shown or is not claimed.
tags.human_gate: A decision a person must make before anything proceeds (approval, release gate).

Specified as a read-only checker of synthetic aircraft maintenance records. It is not specified to certify, release or determine airworthiness. A named human would decide.
The design says a rules engine decides every finding. An optional local language model may only read free text, cannot remove or downgrade a rule finding, and is off by default.
Pass and fail criteria for 70 tests, T01 to T70, are written down and fingerprinted with SHA-256 before Stage 0. They have not been run.

A release check for agent spending on NEAR testnet. The vault holds the NEAR. The agent holds only a function call key that can ask for a spend. The contract pays only when the receiver is allowlisted and the amount fits the per transaction cap and the daily cap. Anything else waits for the owner, or is denied.

This figure is from crs-ai-agents, CRS Pilot 0, an advisory evaluation. It is not a result for the Agent CRS vault, and it is not a result for airworthiness-mcp. Each of three models caught the seeded fault in 16 of 16 tries (8 faulty packs, run twice).

crs-ai-agents reports false alarms on the clean twins as a separate measure, not as part of the 16 of 16 detection line. The repository summarises those false alarms as 19% to 50%. Each reported 16 is eight faulty packs with two epochs, recorded on a first run and on a second run. With 16 trials the Wilson lower bound is 0.81, so the detection line means no misses were seen on those packs. The second run repaired some clean twins after the first results were seen. The pilot is small and self-registered. It is not a certification tool.
The board is not hosted. The repository starts it locally with npm run dev from the web directory. The public evidence is the NEAR testnet vault and a 68 second demo video in docs/demo.
The repository documents 26 contract tests and 4 parser tests. The recorded demo states that no model was called.
Built by Isaac Adekunle / Drew & Crew with AI coding agents, for NEAR Hackathon 2026.

Testnet only. The repository says this is not custody advice and it does not hold mainnet funds. The name is an analogy for a human release check, not a certification, and it is not affiliated with any aviation authority.

At the 7 October 2026 audit checkpoint recorded in the public case study: 95 candidate academy records, 35 verified category classifications, 7 general venue points meeting the category-and-venue filter, and 72 Node tests passed. The case study says these are not continuously updated production metrics, and that 35 classifications do not mean 35 fully verified academy records.

At the 7 October 2026 checkpoint the case study records the runtime stack as React, TypeScript, MapLibre, Vinext, a Cloudflare Worker and D1. Python, FastAPI and PostGIS are described there as separate exploration, not the live research backend.
The public site offers an England postcode search with checked journeys of up to 60 minutes by car, and bus estimates alongside. No account is needed to search. Checked 15 November 2026.

The public site says missing evidence never becomes a zero accessibility score. The case study records an earlier screen that showed 0/100 for a small sample, and the correction that withholds that broader score.

I originated the problem, defined the audience and comparison brief, chose the brand and domains, and directed AI-assisted specification, prototyping and review. The case study says implementation commits are recorded under Codex, and that the 7 October audit was assistant-executed under my instructions. No runtime language model is claimed in the product.
